Messages.Author: GreyB
Messages.Body:
> Wand wrote:
> Guys, if a unleash declares a block uppon a Vampire with signet, what happens?
>
Unleash Hell's Fury
+1 stealth action. Requires an infernal vampire. Unique.
Daimoinon Put this card in play. This card may attempt to block a  action against you and is considered a 9-capacity infernal vampire with +2 intercept during that attempt; if successful, the acting minion takes 1 unpreventable aggravated damage, and this card is burned.
Daimoinon As above, and untap this vampire.

Signet of King Saul, The
Unique equipment.
Vampires with capacity above 7 cannot attempt to block this minion.

Unleash cannot declare a block, since it's (considered) capacity 9.

-1 Strength

Messages.Author: kschaefer
Messages.Body:
EDIT: Last comment was at the top of the page, so I thought this was a new question.

> Name: The Signet of King Saul
> Cardtype: Equipment
> Cost: 1 pool
> Unique equipment.
> Vampires with capacity above 7 cannot attempt to block this minion.
>
> Name: Unleash Hell's Fury
> Cardtype: Action
> Cost: 2 pool
> Discipline: Daimoinon
> Burn Option
> +1 stealth action. Requires an infernal vampire. Unique.
> [dai] Put this card in play. This card can attempt to block a  action against you and is considered a 9-capacity infernal vampire with +2 intercept during that attempt; if successful, the acting minion takes 1 unpreventable aggravated damage, and this card is burned.
> [DAI] As above, and unlock this vampire.
>
Unleash Hell's Fury cannot attempt to block a minion with Signet of King Saul, since UHF is a 9-cap when performing capacity checks (older, younger, above, below, etc.).

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
Vampires with capacity above 7 cannot attempt to block this minion.
This card can attempt to block a  action against you and is considered a 9-capacity infernal vampire

The two cards interact with each other in the clearest way possible since they use exactly the same terms.

If an effect says "X can do Y", and another effect says "X cannot do Y", then the "cannot" effect takes precedence over the "can" effect.

Prince of Paris, France

Messages.Author: Bloodartist
Messages.Body:
> Mewcat wrote:
> I think the question is more broadly about cards that are 1 thing but become something else in a limited capacity and sequencing. When do they begin being the new thing? When do they stop?
>
The key here is that unleash attempts to block AS a 9-cap vampire. There is not a moment where its not a vampire, attempts to block and turns into a vampire... At least in my opinion.

> Mewcat wrote:
> Assumptions:
> seduction can not be played on unleash hells fury
> unleash hells fury cannot be chosen in terms on referendum
>
Seduction cannot be played on unleash, because seduction is played AS THE ACTION IS ANNOUNCED. I can never remember was a bleed action card even replaced when seduction must be played, but at any rate at the same time you announce the bleed action. Nobody has a chance to declare blockers at that point, therefore unleash is not a vampire. Seduction can be DI'd (etc. canceled) because DI MUST be played at that same window.

Unleash is only considered a vampire when it attempts to block.

The sequence of windows when different cards can be played is actually quite long and something I have complained about..

> You play Concealed Weapon, wait for DIs, draw, then play the weapon that you intend to conceal (cannot be canceled by any current game effects), then you draw.
>
Correct.

You can put aside, face down, the weapon you are equipping as a sign you have indeed a weapon in you hand when you play Concealed Weapon, but you cannot show it until the Concealed Weapon is resolved successfully.

Playing both Concealed Weapon and the weapon face up, at the same time, before replacing both is illegal.
